confidence: Behavior confirmed; defect classification depends on the intended approximation contract
title: A relatively curved tiny spine is classified as linear
trigger: A quadratic Bezier spine with poles (0,0,0),(5e-11,4e-11,0),(1e-10,0,0) is accepted as an X-axis line. Its midpoint is (5e-11,2e-11,0): 20% of the chord off that line.
impact: The collinearity tolerance is 1e-10*max(extent,1). It dominates this entire spine and can enable cylinder classification. The absolute error is only 2e-11 mm, so whether this is wrong depends on whether this owner promises exact analytic recognition or an allowed absolute approximation.
repair: Decide and document that contract. For exact recognition, use a scale-relative criterion or source error bounds. If absolute approximation is intended, retain it explicitly and do not describe the replacement as exact.
verification: asm::curved_spine_becomes_line; complete extracted classifier and checked NURBS evaluation.
limit: Policy-dependent observation, not counted as a confirmed numerical defect. Tiny physical dimensions; downstream complete rolling-ball transfer was not executed.
relation_to_prior_audits: Different owner or failure mechanism from the earlier reported witnesses.

title: A short witnessed arc is replaced by a full circle
trigger: A unit circle with endpoints at angles 0 and 0.001 radians and an interior witness at 0.0005 returns [0, TAU]. Its endpoint separation is about 0.001 mm, below the 0.002 mm endpoint threshold.
impact: The proximity shortcut runs before angular or witness checks. A small edge can gain almost one full turn; the witness already distinguishes the short arc. This is not a last-bit normalization difference.
repair: Use source closure information or a distinct angular/witness decision for full turns. Endpoint proximity alone cannot establish closure.
verification: catia::short_witnessed_arc_becomes_full_circle; complete extracted function and its actual helpers, checked IR circle.
limit: No complete codec decode or export was run.
relation_to_prior_audits: The sixth-pass repair stabilized standard_analytic_curve_angle at extreme radii. This is the caller’s separate full-turn shortcut.

title: Plane–circle intersection returns the circle center for a secant
trigger: For circle center (0,0,0), axis Z, radius 1e-7, and plane x=0, the function returns only (0,0,0). The exact intersections are (0,+1e-7,0) and (0,-1e-7,0).
impact: The squared radial remainder is compared with 1e-12*max(radius,1)^2 and classified as tangent. The result is not on the circle. intersection_resolve uses this owner when cutting carrier-intersection circles by a plane.
repair: Use a dimensionless radial comparison and a stable half-chord; classify multiplicity independently of a 1 mm floor.
verification: creo::tiny_plane_circle_returns_center; complete extracted function with production vector helpers.
limit: No complete codec decode or export was run.
relation_to_prior_audits: Earlier fixes covered trim/sketch circle solvers and surface candidate constructors. This is the separate analytic plane-cut owner.

title: Tiny disjoint sphere supports manufacture a tangent point
trigger: Radius-1e-10 spheres at x=0 and x=3e-10 return the midpoint x=1.5e-10 although they are disjoint. A sphere at x=3e-10 with radius 1e-10 and plane x=0 returns the origin. point_on_carrier accepts these false candidates against the sphere supports.
impact: The pair constructors use an absolute 1e-9 floor and the final carrier gate uses an even larger absolute 1e-7 floor. solve_carriers_with_diagnostics therefore cannot remove these false pair candidates at its final membership check.
repair: Use support-scaled tangency and membership residuals. Any absolute model tolerance must be explicit and must not silently turn a disjoint pair into a unique exact tangent.
verification: creo::disjoint_tiny_spheres_invent_tangent; complete extracted tangent and membership functions.
limit: Very small model lengths; constructor and final membership behavior reproduced. The complete triple-carrier solver was inspected, not executed.
relation_to_prior_audits: Different owner or failure mechanism from the earlier reported witnesses.

impact: Valid candidates are rejected by the common final membership gate. Cylinder radial distance and the torus tube-distance arm contain the same unscaled squared-norm construction.
repair: Use robust norms in each arm and stable radial projection where needed. Keep this range repair separate from the small-radius tolerance policy.
verification: creo::large_sphere_point_is_refused; complete function, sphere arm executed; cylinder and torus copies confirmed in source.

title: Remaining section collectors duplicate an existing collector policy
trigger: prototype_pcurves and curve_prototype_topology have the same identifier-normalized loop: decode each section, relocate offsets, append, sort. The listed siblings repeat that traversal with different relocation closures or section filters.
impact: collect_section_records already owns this policy and accepts the decoder, relocation and ordering operations. The remaining loops duplicate that owner without adding a traversal guarantee. No runtime defect is asserted.
repair: Route these collectors through the existing helper. Preserve each relocation field and section predicate. two_chart_pcurves can reuse the collection prefix while retaining its distinct uniqueness filter; datum_planes must retain its additional named-plane record.
verification: Source and AST comparison only; no behavior change or runtime reproduction.
limit: This is one maintenance family, not one finding per function. Typed getters and representation-specific conversions are excluded.
relation_to_prior_audits: CREO3-05 and CREO4-02 migrated other collectors. These remaining bodies still contain the common loop.

impact: project_move writes rotation=None into MoveBody. The source contains a resolvable rotation, but the feature projection loses it.
repair: Recover the small angle from both the skew part and trace with atan2, while retaining the half-turn axis branch.

title: Endpoint snapping collapses an exact pcurve domain
trigger: A valid degree-one pcurve with knots [0,0,1e-10,1e-10] and range [0,1e-10] returns [0,0]. Both endpoints are within the floored 1e-9 tolerance of the lower knot; the lower comparison wins even for an exact upper endpoint.
impact: The stored pcurve range is corrupted. The edge-use path also drops the range because bounded_pcurve_range requires a strict increase. Small parameter intervals do not imply small model geometry: the probe’s poles span one parameter-space unit.
repair: Preserve exact endpoint matches first; then snap to an unambiguous nearest boundary with a tolerance bounded by the domain separation.

title: Periodic knot extension overflows a cancellable period
trigger: For degree 1 and periodic knots [-1e308,-9e307,9e307,1e308], the function returns Ok with exterior knots -infinity and +infinity. The correct exterior values are -1.1e308 and +1.1e308, both representable.
impact: Computing last-first first overflows, although each final three-term sum is finite. Text and binary curve/pcurve paths and surface knot normalization share this owner; later finite-knot admission refuses the result.
repair: Compute each exterior knot with a scaled or cancellation-safe sum; reject only an unrepresentable final knot.

title: Common rational weight scaling changes closest-point projection
trigger: A line from (0,0,0) to (1,0,0), queried at x=0.25, has residual controls [-0.25*w,0,0,w] and [0.75*w,0,0,w]. Common weights 1 give a nonconstant derivative; 1e200 returns None; 1e-200 returns all zeros. The endpoint residual becomes infinity or zero instead of 0.25.
impact: The NURBS geometry is unchanged by a common weight factor. Raw Bernstein products and residual squares make projection depend on that arbitrary representation factor; the production caller accepts these finite positive weights.
repair: Normalize homogeneous controls before polynomial products and use a robust dehomogenized residual norm. Preserve root ordering and the existing work budget.
verification: nx::common_weight_scale_changes_projection; actual derivative-product and distance helpers; checked NURBS constructor and IR evaluation control.
limit: Extreme common weight factors with ordinary point coordinates. Full budgeted root isolation was not run.
relation_to_prior_audits: Different owner or failure mechanism from the earlier reported witnesses.

title: Shallow extrusion miters lose their tilt through acos
trigger: active_miter accepts normal (1e-8,0,1). Its normalized Z rounds to 1; acos(Z) becomes zero. Transforming (1e8,0,0) leaves Z=0, with a 1 mm residual against the intended miter plane instead of Z approximately -1.
impact: The input retains a finite transverse normal component, but profile point and basis construction discard the tilt. The error grows with profile extent.
repair: Recover the angle with atan2(hypot(normal.x,normal.y),normal.z), or use a direct stable miter map.
verification: rhino::shallow_miter_tilt_is_lost; full admission, normalization, miter and Rodrigues helpers; error-carrier stub.
limit: Angle 1e-8 radians. The 1 mm residual witness uses a 1e8 mm profile extent; a 1 mm profile has a 1e-8 mm error.
relation_to_prior_audits: Different owner or failure mechanism from the earlier reported witnesses.

title: Source-less angular validation still rejects valid short and shallow lines
trigger: Two perpendicular segments of length 1e-5 are rejected as degenerate because their length product 1e-10 is compared against the linear 1e-9 threshold. Unit-length lines at angle 1e-8 instead measure as zero through acos and fail the final 1e-9 agreement test.
impact: The source-less writer refuses valid dimensions. This is a separate angle implementation from the already repaired relation-record helper, with both a dimensional mismatch and small-angle cancellation.
repair: Check each line length against the linear gate, then compute the angle from normalized cross and dot with atan2. Share the established angle policy where ownership allows.
verification: sld::valid_angular_dimensions_are_refused; verbatim numeric block from the Angle arm and vector2_length, with a Result wrapper and error stub.
limit: The numeric branch and final comparison were reproduced; complete source-less export was not run.
relation_to_prior_audits: SLDPRT6-01 repaired relation_records::line_line_angle. This independent writer branch still uses the old arithmetic.

title: Finite mesh mass properties are lost when centroid moments overflow
trigger: Scale the tetrahedron (0,0,0),(2,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1) by 1e90. Its area, volume (1e270/3), and centroid (5e89,2.5e89,2.5e89) are finite, but mesh_properties returns None because volume-weighted centroid terms overflow.
impact: The validation-property reader loses its computed comparison values. Moving the origin fixed translation cancellation, but does not bound the fourth-power centroid moment intermediates.
repair: Accumulate in a scaled local coordinate system and rescale area, volume and centroid separately; use stable summation for many triangles.
verification: step::finite_mass_properties_are_lost; complete function with minimal body/mesh containers exposing the same fields and slices. Unit-scale tetrahedron is the control.
limit: Extreme finite model scale. No full STEP validation-property import was run.
relation_to_prior_audits: STEP2-01 repaired translation dependence. This is uniform-scale overflow in the remaining moment accumulation.

title: Circle intersection loses the smaller circle at unequal scales
trigger: A unit circle at the origin and a radius-1e200 circle centered at (1e200,0) return a single point (0,0). Analytically they have two intersections near (5e-201,+1) and (5e-201,-1). The returned center is not on the unit circle.
impact: After scaling by the large circle, the small radius is 1e-200 and its square underflows. The height becomes zero and two finite roots collapse to a false tangent. This shared helper is used by codec and IR intersection owners.
repair: Preserve independent radial scales and evaluate the half-chord without squaring away the small radius. Include strongly unequal circles, not only common scaling.
verification: planar::unequal_circles_intersect_at_wrong_center; complete current function and current finite-sum implementation.
limit: Extreme radius ratio. No claim that ordinary comparable circles fail.
relation_to_prior_audits: The earlier planar repair handled common extreme scaling. This witness changes the ratio between the two radii.

title: Normalized-vector derivatives are refused after intermediate overflow
trigger: vector=(1,1,1), derivative=(MAX,MAX,MAX) returns None. The normalized vector is constant along this parallel derivative, so its derivative is zero. vector=(MAX,MAX,0) with zero derivative is also refused although its unit direction is finite.
impact: The raw projection unit.dot(derivative), or the full vector length, overflows before a finite normalized result can be formed. Sweep and rolling-ball differential evaluation consume this helper.
repair: Scale the vector and derivative independently and form the projected derivative with stable products and sums; preserve representable final normalized derivatives.
verification: eval::parallel_derivative_is_refused; complete function plus actual offset/vector-sum helpers.
limit: Extreme finite derivatives or vector magnitudes; no full procedural surface evaluation was run.
relation_to_prior_audits: Different owner or failure mechanism from the earlier reported witnesses.

repair: Reuse the stable transform or finite-dot operation for both point and derivative transformation. Remove the duplicated raw product-sum policy.
verification: eval::proper_rotation_produces_nonfinite_rail; both complete helpers plus proper-rigid validation and stable-transform comparison.
